Most significantly, the convention for the Pauli sigma $z$ matrix is that $\sigma_{z}|0\rangle=|0\rangle$ and $\sigma_{z}|1\rangle=-|1\rangle$, which is reverse of what some physicists (but usually not computer scientists or mathematicians) intuitively expect. The origin of this dissonance is that the +1 eigenstate of $\sigma_{z}$ is often identified by physicists with a so-called 'excited state', and it seems natural to many to identify this with $|1\rangle$, rather than with $|0\rangle$ as is done in this book.
